episodes.200090: A southward moving cold front out of the Ohio Valley to southern Mid-Atlantic region combined with a weak disturbance aloft to produce isolated to scattered showers and storms over central North Carolina in the late afternoon and evening. The strongest storms produced quarter to ping pong ball size hail over the western to eastern Piedmont. A few damaging wind reports were also observed.
episodes.200438: Despite the absence of large scale lift over West Texas, numerous severe thunderstorms were able to form on the afternoon of the 22nd. Strong surface heating existed along and east of a diffuse dryline roughly around the US Highway 385 corridor. Low level moisture return east of the dryline combined with steep mid level lapse rates to create an unstable atmosphere by mid-afternoon. Veering and increasing winds with height allowed some storms to become organized and produced large hail and damaging wind gusts. The initial activity developed over the south-central Texas Panhandle, with additional development farther southwestward into the western South Plains. Large hail up to tennis ball size and gusty outflow winds were common with the strongest storms. One particularly intense storm approached the Matador area (Motley County). This storm was rotating rapidly aloft but never produced a tornado.
episodes.200536: Scattered thunderstorms moved across parts of northwest Illinois during the evening of April 22nd producing isolated large hail.
episodes.200722: A broad trough across the western United States and a dryline across the Permian Basin and Stockton Plateau resulted in afternoon thunderstorms. Several severe right-moving supercells occurred over the Stockton Plateau, with left-moving supercells moving across western portions of the Permian Basin. In addition, a localized dry microburst resulted in intense wind gusts of 100 MPH or greater near Midland International Air & Space Port.
episodes.200834: Showers developed ahead of an area of low pressure across central Minnesota in the Brainerd Lakes area during the early morning hours of the 22nd. Activity was mainly showers with limited instability present. One shower did produce some isolated lightning, including a few positive bolts. One of these positive bolts struck a large tree just south of Loon Lake near the town of Pequot Lakes and caused extensive damage to homes along a cul-de-sac.
episodes.201127: A fast-moving shortwave trough and its associated surface front advanced into eastern Nebraska on the evening of April 21, 2025. A broken line of elevated thunderstorms developed along the front, which was positioned across east-central Nebraska. Modest instability, combined with steep sub-cloud lapse rates, supported several reports of severe hail ranging from 1 to 1.75 inches in diameter. However, the storms quickly weakened as they moved into Iowa later in the evening.
episodes.201261: Widely scattered thunderstorms developed well ahead of a cold front across the Illinois River Valley during the afternoon of April 22nd.  One of the cells dropped quarter-sized hail in northern Fulton County.
episodes.201358: An isolated severe thunderstorm developed across the Upstate of SC and caused some tree damage in Lancaster County. A weak shortwave trough aloft, moving into a region with modest instability and mid-level dry air helped developed an isolated downburst.
episodes.201708: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours of April 22nd east of the dryline. The combination of instability, abundant low level moisture and wind shear allowed storms to become severe and produce hail up to ping pong ball size in the southeast Texas Panhandle. A similar setup occurred on April 23rd where the dryline was situated a little further west which allowed for storms to develop across more of the combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles. Gusty winds and hail up to tennis ball size occurred on the 23rd as storms moved west.
episodes.201877: A cold front moved into the region and stalled late in April producing a few days of rain. Flooding occurred at multiple locations and severe storms also developed as a result.
episodes.202052: A line of severe thunderstorms lifted north northeastward along the Mississippi River through the Quad Cites with an area of trailing stratiform rainfall behind it. There were scattered reports of thunderstorm wind damage in the counties along the Mississippi River. A microburst occurred near West Burlington that caused damage to  a DOT Shet and broke several power poles. An NWS Storm Survey team found damage in this area consistent with wind speeds of 80 to 90 mph. In addition to the severe thunderstorms, heavy rainfall of 2 to 3 inches fell across western Johnson and southwest Linn Counties. This led to reports of flash flooding in western Cedar Rapids, Hiawatha, and Marion.
episodes.202208: A warm front lifted north across Lower East Texas to along the Arkansas/Louisiana border during the afternoon of April 22nd, allowing for the return of warmer, more humid air back north across portions of East Texas and much of North Louisiana. This resulted in ample instability during the afternoon, as an upper level disturbance embedded in the developing southwest flow aloft from the Texas Hill Country into the Lower Mississippi Valley progressed northeast across the area. Sufficient wind shear was also available, and combined with the strong instability, resulted in the development of scattered supercell thunderstorms across portions of Northcentral Louisiana. These storms produced large hail across portions of Natchitoches, Grant, and Ouachita Parishes, before shifting northeast into Northeast Louisiana by early evening.
episodes.202309: Isolated severe storms occurred across south central Virginia during the late afternoon as some instability was able to develop as clouds thinned.
episodes.202353: On the afternoon of April 21st, a cold front approaching the region began to stall over central Louisiana as upper-level support and steering flow shifted northeastward. With the front losing its dynamical push, storms developed ahead of it across the New Orleans area and became slow-moving due to the lack of steering flow. These storms produced efficient, long-duration rainfall over the city, and the urban landscape of New Orleans quickly became overwhelmed. The result was widespread flash flooding across the metro area, which persisted until the rain finally tapered off near sunset.
episodes.202355: On April 22nd, the same cold front from the previous day began retreating northward into northern Louisiana, placing the region back in the warm sector with unstable air. With dry air aloft and favorable mid-level lapse rates, a strong storm developed across the Florida Parishes during the afternoon. The storm produced severe hail near Zachary before gradually weakening as it moved southeast.
episodes.202381: An area of showers with isolated embedded thunderstorms moved across northwest South Carolina during the afternoon in advance of a cold front. One isolated severe storm produced damaging wind gusts and hail in Chester County.
episodes.202684: Severe storms produced hail ranging from quarter to ping pong ball size across central and southeast Mississippi. Several vehicles sustained damage as a result of the hail.

A positive bolt of lightning struck a large red pine tree on a cul-de-sac on the south side of Loon Lake just southeast of the town of Pequot Lakes. The bolt caused extensive damage to one of the homes on the cul-de-sac including blowing out two well systems, burning the electric lines into the home, damaged a water line along with a water heater and water softener, blew off multiple tongue and groove boards, insulation and soffit on the house and a shed, destroyed internet and phone lines and all equipment connected to it, and had several wires burn and melt, leading to a smoky haze in the home. All of the homes on the cul-de-sac had some degree of damage, ranging from blown outlets to warped soffit pieces to blown out wells.
